page: Amazon Web Services c7g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARM architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, operating without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The server includes hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES support, provides a 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark data highlights strong multithreaded and memory subsystem metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark memory score in the top 10% bracket, supported by large-block memory read bandwidth of 249.33 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 105.99 GB/sec (both in the top 25%). Compute workloads show solid parallel efficiency, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,547.0 and high throughput in PassMark database operations and physics testing. Networking and static data distribution are demonstrated by a static web serving throughput of 48.85 GB/sec.

Hardware tradeoffs center around memory density, storage architecture, and accelerator capabilities. With 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory-intensive working sets may become constrained. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires external network-attached block storage for persistence. Furthermore, while the instance executes small and medium LLM inference smoothly via CPU, prompt processing throughput on 70B models drops into the bottom 10%, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

In qualitative terms, the physical core dedication and memory bandwidth offer high resource efficiency for compute-bound tasks without SMT contention. Amazon Web Services c7g.8xlarge is well aligned for distributed web serving tiers, software compilation, batch compute pipelines, containerized microservices, and high-concurrency database workloads that match its compute-to-memory ratio.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated physical cores running on 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture at 2.6 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. It delivers 64.0 GB of system memory, providing an exact 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, supported by 15 Gbps baseline networking throughput. The platform contains no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier memory subsystem performance, reaching the top 10% in PassMark memory testing and top 25% in uncached read and write throughput, alongside strong multi-core processing in Geekbench and PassMark database operations. However, large-model AI inference is constrained due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators. Qualitatively, the architecture offers solid compute density and throughput efficiency for container fleets, clustered compute jobs, high-traffic web servers, and distributed continuous integration pipelines.
